status: mechanism challenge complete; direct cipher corpus experiment still requires source recovery

memory_horizon.question: Does line0 add coupling-free prospective information about absolute future line states?
memory_horizon.design: 5-fold physical-leaf CV; for horizon h, baseline uses metadata plus immediately preceding line when h>1; test additionally uses line0; target is absolute line h fingerprint.
memory_horizon.decision: No detectable prospective structural memory carried by line0 beyond metadata/previous-line state. Even line1 absolute state is not improved reliably. The surviving entry phenomenon is best treated as a position/register specialization rather than a persistent initializer.

frozen_phase50_dsl_challenge.generator: Phase50 frozen DSL family: nroots=64, block=4, state_use=.30, prefix_p=.22, suffix_p=.32, variants_per_root=2. Generator is not informed of paragraph boundaries; empirical Voynich paragraph/line lengths retained.
frozen_phase50_dsl_challenge.target: real-entry minus internal-pseudo two-line structural transition, projected on frozen Voynich direction
frozen_phase50_dsl_challenge.decision: P60-5 survives against the frozen stationary/weakly contextual DSL. The generator can produce multivariate fluctuations of comparable raw norm, but they are not concentrated at genuine paragraph entries and point almost orthogonally to the Voynich entry-specific direction.

bounded_cipher_analysis.scope: Fixed low-complexity encodings applied globally, without access to paragraph position: monoalphabetic bijection, fixed homophonic substitution, and fixed token-codebook substitution.
bounded_cipher_analysis.mechanism_result: These transforms cannot create a paragraph-conditioned mechanism ex nihilo. A monoalphabetic bijection exactly preserves token equality, token length, sequence positions, inventory cardinality/entropy up to symbol renaming, and the edit-distance-1 graph under symbol relabeling. Fixed homophonic or codebook transforms can change surface statistics, but without boundary access any systematic entry/body difference must be inherited from the plaintext token/register distribution rather than generated by the cipher itself.
bounded_cipher_analysis.decision: P60-6 is NOT a discriminator against ordinary globally applied simple ciphers. Phase59 already shows that meaningful medieval plaintext can contain a source-entry register partly aligned with Voynich. A simple position-independent cipher would preserve/inherit such document structure rather than erase it. Therefore the observed entry register is compatible with encrypted meaningful text, but is not positive evidence for encryption. To make ciphering explanatory rather than merely compatible, a candidate cipher must predict additional Voynich-specific morphology/near-family/edge structure beyond what its plaintext already contains.
bounded_cipher_analysis.direct_experiment_status: The exact external Latin source texts used in Phase59B are not present in the current local runtime/repository, so fresh encrypted-corpus re-tokenization was not fabricated. Recovering those exact source inputs is required for a direct numerical transform experiment.

supported: P60-1: real paragraph boundaries differ from matched internal pseudo-boundaries
P60-2: entry specialization has stable structural carriers
P60-3: a formal entry/body role transfers across major sections
P60-5: frozen stationary/weakly contextual DSL without explicit entry machinery fails the entry-specific direction
not_supported_or_revised: P60-4: persistent entry initialization of later body state is not supported
P60-6 as originally hoped is not discriminative: simple global ciphers can inherit plaintext entry grammar and therefore cannot be rejected from entry structure alone
phase60_decision.open: P60-7 independent localized content relation remains untested/blocked by mapping quality.

interpretation: The strongest surviving statement is architectural, not semantic: Voynich text generation is document-structure-aware at paragraph entry. Meaningless formal generation remains viable only if it includes explicit boundary-conditioned machinery. Meaningful plaintext plus a simple global cipher remains viable because medieval plaintext itself can carry entry/register structure. The next discriminator must target Voynich-specific morphology or independently grounded localized content, not merely the existence of paragraph entry structure.
next: Phase61 should compare two explicit architectures on unseen constraints: (A) boundary-aware nonsemantic generator and (B) structured medieval plaintext plus globally applied encoding. Freeze joint targets including entry signature, near-family density/local continuity, line-position grammar, section modulation and absence of persistent entry memory. Prefer source recovery for the exact Phase59 Latin controls before numerical cipher simulation.
